request.spec:
A steward can roll the year over: a year entry and a button. It generates the next fiscal year's
twelve periods exactly as the fiscal year generator does, and for each person their open figure at
the end of the old year's last period (the due of their claims that count, belonging to a period of
the old year, OPEN or PENDING at that period's end) is added to their carried figure for the new
year's first period as OPENING_SET lines; then ROLLOVER fy=<old FY> periods=<made> is written. A year
with no periods, anyone but a steward, or a bad year is refused with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can roll the year over: a year entry and a button. It generates the next fiscal year's
twelve periods exactly as the fiscal year generator does, and for each person their open figure at
the end of the old year's last period (the due of their claims that count, belonging to a period of
the old year, OPEN or PENDING at that period's end) is added to their carried figure for the new
year's first period as OPENING_SET lines; then ROLLOVER fy=<old FY> periods=<made> is written. A year
with no periods, anyone but a steward, or a bad year is refused with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the year-end rollover. The main rollover test passes, but `bin/e2e` is not fully green: 3 of the 4 tests in the spec pass, and "year end rollover scenario 2" fails.

**What's added**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/rollover`, taking `{"year":"yyyy"}`:
  - **Refusals:** a year that isn't `yyyy` gets a 400. A user who isn't a steward, or a year with no periods, gets a 409. A refusal stores nothing and writes nothing to the audit file.
  - **New periods:** it makes the next fiscal year's twelve months the same way the fiscal year generator does, logged as `PERIOD_ADDED` lines.
  - **Openings:** for each person it takes their open figure at the end of the old year's last period. That is the due of their claims that count, belong to an old-year period, and were OPEN or PENDING on that period's last day. It adds that figure to their opening balance for the new year's first period and logs an `OPENING_SET` line.
  - **Audit:** it finishes with `ROLLOVER fy=FY<yyyy> periods=<made>`.
  - The work is mainly in `ValidateRollover.java`, `SetRolloverOpenings.java` and a new `personOpenAt` method in `Rollup.java`.
- **Front end:** `features/periods/rollover.slot.tsx` adds the `rollover-year` input, the `rollover` button, the `rollover-made` count and `rollover-error`, placed below the opening-balance import.

**Two choices of mine**
- A person whose open figure is 0.00 gets no `OPENING_SET` line. The request doesn't say either way and the test doesn't check it.
- If the new year's first month already existed, so it wasn't generated, the openings go to whichever existing period contains that first day.

**The failing test**
Scenario 2 never uses the rollover. It fails on `rate-month-C-2026-04`, expecting `12.50` and getting `n/a`, while viewing the sheet as of 2026-03-20. From reading the code, I think the failure comes from the real date on this machine, not from my change:
- The 12.50 should come from the parent sheet `<sheet>-p`. That parent never stores a "today".
- The history journal (`Journal.java`) stamps changes to a sheet with no stored today with the real date, which is 2026-10-30.
- So when the sheet is viewed as of 2026-03-20, the parent's rates look like they don't exist yet, and the cell shows `n/a`.

My guess is the test passed when the real date was earlier. I didn't run it without my change to confirm it was already failing. I also didn't change that rule, because it's outside this request and would change how every "as of" view reads parent sheets. If you want, I can make the journal fall back to something other than the real date for sheets with no stored today.
